dedupe_keys.name: sispea national observatory of water and sanitation services france

description: SISPEA is the national observatory of public drinking water and sanitation services in France, run by the French Biodiversity Office to give an overall view of how services are organised and perform, to guide national water policy and to inform users. Local authorities, their contractors and operators enter data each year, and since January 2025 SISPEA is also the single tool for the technical data used to modulate water agencies' drinking water performance levy. The open data section offers the full set of validated data: annual data for each drinking water, collective sanitation and non-collective sanitation service, including service and works descriptions, descriptive and performance indicators and the variables that compute them; the commune composition of every service for mapping; the organising authorities; and annual tariffs. Files span 2008 to 2026 as XLS or ODS, roughly 10 MB per year for drinking water, regenerated every weekend. Reuse falls under the Etalab Licence Ouverte for public information, at no cost. Caveats: reporting is self-declared and incomplete for small services, and the latest years fill in as the campaign progresses. Simulation uses: parameterising leakage, network renewal, service reliability and cost in drinking water and sewer models, comparing service performance and optimising investments. Related records: Hub'Eau (data-hubeau-french-water-data-apis) exposes the indicators by API; comparable national benchmarking sets are Australia's National Performance Report (data-bom-national-performance-report-urban-water) and Brazil's SNIS (data-brazil-snis-sanitation-information-system).
